tessa: Bringing up lilac-embed-v2 int8 smoke on staging — quick numbers show a drop on short queries (recall@1). sharing raw snapshot.

 tessa: Quick metrics (holdout anchor set, 10k calib samples):
 `Recall@1: fp16 0.82 -> int8 0.75`
 `Recall@5: fp16 0.94 -> int8 0.92`
 `Mean cosine: fp16 0.317 -> int8 0.347 (shift +0.03)`
 `Cluster purity (kmeans, 100 anchors): 0.88 -> 0.81`

 sam: ugh that's bigger than i expected for r@1. did you use per-channel or per-tensor quant?

 tessa: per-channel symmetric, no outlier clipping. calibration set = 10k random queries + contexts.

 maria: do we normalize vectors before recall? that cosine shift could be from scale change after quant.

 tessa: baseline pipeline does l2 normalize after encoding. int8 path currently skips a final fp32 scale correction (possible bug).

 chris: can you paste the eval command you ran? i want to repro locally.

 tessa: `python eval_embeddings.py --model lilac-embed-v2 --quant int8 --calib 10k --holdout anchors_5k.json --normalize True --k 10`

 dev-bot: run-12345 finished — attached quick CSV: r1=0.75,r5=0.92,mean_cos=0.347,cluster_purity=0.81

 sam: two quick experiments to try:
 - per-tensor asymmetric quant (lower dynamic range error for tail activations)
 - apply range-clipping at 99.9th percentile before quant

 maria: also try re-normalizing embeddings after quant (i.e. force unit norm) and rerun recall@1 stratified by query length.

 chris: i think we should check whitening/mean-centering step too. baseline had optional whitening turned on for some evals.

 tessa: plan: I'll run per-tensor asymmetric + clip @99.9 on the 5k anchor holdout. Sam can try whitening + post-quant l2 norm. Maria will prepare stratified shortquery set (<=16 tokens). target to have results by EOD.

 sam: if post-quant l2 norm recovers ~<2% r@1 delta, we can consider shipping int8 with forced unit-norm as a mitigation.

 maria: noted — prepping shortquery split now.

 tessa: also flagging for infra: kv-cache paths seem fine but will run a few sample end-to-end inference checks for context bleed.

 chris: thanks all. cc @eng-ml — if we see persistent centroid drift after these fixes we may need to revert int8 rollouts for Lilac.

 tessa: updated — running jobs now. will drop logs here when done :hourglass_flowing_sand:

 sam: :eyes:
